title: Sell Mineral Rights in Plaza, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Plaza, ND
metaDescription: Mineral rights near Plaza, ND in Mountrail County? Core Bakken acreage with real production history. Get an honest, well-informed offer.
heroLead: Plaza sits in central Mountrail County, close enough to the Parshall and Sanish fields that a lot of local mineral interests have real production behind them, even if the town itself stays out of the headlines.
intro: Families who've held mineral rights around Plaza since the original homestead days have generally watched the same pattern play out that hit most of central Mountrail County after 2006: a wave of leasing, then drilling, then years of steady, declining royalty checks. Where exactly your acreage sits relative to the field's best wells makes a real difference in what it's worth today.

sections.heading: Central Mountrail County's production history
paragraphs: This part of the county has seen dense horizontal development since the Bakken boom began, with many spacing units supporting multiple wellbores across both the Bakken and Three Forks zones. We check exactly which wells are tied to your tract before pricing anything.

sections.heading: What we need to give you an honest number
paragraphs: A recent royalty statement or Division Order tells us the most, since it shows us which well and which decimal interest you actually hold. Without one, we can still research your tract through the Mountrail County Recorder and the state's well records, it just takes a bit more time.

sections.heading: Family ownership around Plaza over the generations
paragraphs: Plaza's mineral ownership tends to follow the same pattern as the rest of central Mountrail County: an original homesteader, a lease signed sometime after 2006, and an interest that's since passed to children and grandchildren, sometimes without a formal deed reflecting every current owner.
We handle that title work directly rather than ask you to sort it out yourself, confirming the real ownership picture through the county recorder before any offer is made.

faqs.question: We don't have a recent statement. Can you still make an offer?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can research your ownership and well history through county and state records even without a statement in hand, though a statement speeds things up.

faqs.question: Is Plaza close enough to Parshall field to matter for value?
faqs.answer: It depends on your specific section, some Plaza-area tracts sit close to strong production, others further out. We check your exact location before quoting.

faqs.question: How do royalty deductions work on our statement?
faqs.answer: Operators typically deduct gathering, processing, and transportation costs before calculating your net payment. We can walk you through your specific statement line by line.

faqs.question: Our deed only has our grandparents' names on it. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It usually means a probate or affidavit of heirship is needed to reflect the current owners before a sale can close, which we can help arrange.
